name: Australia
targetIntake: Autumn 2027 (May 2027 IB session). In Australia this means either the July 2027 mid-year intake or, more usually, Semester 1 starting late February 2028.
tagline: Three-year degrees, published IB conversion, and a calendar that runs backwards
summary: Australia runs on the southern hemisphere academic year: the main intake, Semester 1, starts in late February or early March, and a smaller second intake starts in July. That means finishing the IB in May 2027 does not lead to an 'autumn 2027' start - it leads either to a July 2027 start, if the university offers your degree mid-year, or to February 2028, which gives you roughly eight months between your IB exams and your first lecture. Most bachelor's degrees are three years, entry is decided almost entirely by a published score, and the Universities Admissions Centre publishes an official table that turns your IB result into an ATAR-equivalent 'Combined Rank'.
whyConsider: The entry rule is a number you can look up. UAC converts your IB score into a Combined Rank comparable with the ATAR, the conversion is national, and universities publish the rank each degree needs.
Three-year bachelor's degrees, so you finish in the same time as in Denmark, and four-year honours only if you choose it.
A degree gives access to the Temporary Graduate visa (subclass 485), Post-Higher Education Work stream, which usually lasts two to three years.
You can work up to 48 hours a fortnight while your course is in session, and full-time during breaks.
The gap between your May 2027 exams and a February 2028 start is long enough for a real job, a language course or travel - which some students want and others hate.

If you are looking at Sydney or Canberra, an IB Diploma puts you inside UAC - one application, one fee, several universities - and UAC is open to a candidate sitting the exams in Europe; the Victorian, South Australian and Western Australian centres are not.
watchOuts: Hemisphere timing. If you start in February 2028 you are effectively taking a gap year. If you find a July 2027 mid-year intake you start almost straight after your exams - but not every degree has one, and engineering and health degrees often do not.

There are two IB conversion tables on UAC's page and the wrong one is the one that looks more precise. The quarter-point IB Admissions Score schedule is only for candidates who sat the IB in Australia. Yours is the whole-number one.

There is no national application portal. New South Wales and the ACT have UAC and will take you; Victoria, South Australia and Western Australia have admissions centres that will not, because their IB route is restricted to candidates sitting the exams in Australia or to residents. Queensland is unresolved. Elsewhere you apply to each university separately.

Cost. International tuition at a research university runs roughly AUD 47,000-57,000 a year for arts and business and considerably more for medicine and veterinary science, and the visa's financial test asks for your actual first-year fee rather than an average.

The student visa is expensive and getting more so: the subclass 500 application charge is from AUD 2,500 as of September 2026, and on top of it you must show AUD 29,710 of living costs for twelve months, the first year of tuition and about AUD 2,000 of travel.
Distance. A return flight to Denmark takes about 24 hours and costs real money; most students fly back once a year at most.

ibRecognition.minimumPoints: There is no national minimum. Entry is decided by a rank, and UAC's published schedule is what turns your IB total into one: for offers made from August 2026, 24 points converts to a Combined Rank of 64.60, 30 to 79.30, 35 to 90.75, 40 to 96.85 and 45 to 99.95. Degrees then state the rank they require, so a course asking for a rank of 90 is asking for roughly IB 34-35. Use the whole table on the destination record rather than these five rows.
ibRecognition.subjectLevelRule: Entry is on the overall converted rank, with named prerequisite subjects on top - typically Mathematics at a specified level for engineering, economics and science, and Chemistry or Biology for health degrees. Whether an SL subject satisfies a prerequisite is decided by the university.
ibRecognition.gradeConversion: UAC converts an IB Diploma into a Combined Rank, which it states is comparable with the ATAR for tertiary entrance in every Australian state and territory. There are two schedules on one page and they give different answers. Candidates who sat the IB in Australia from November 2022 are converted from a fine-grained IB Admissions Score in quarter-point steps; everyone else, including anyone sitting the May session in Denmark, is converted from the whole diploma score out of 45. The schedule underneath both is agreed nationally by the Australasian Conference of Tertiary Admissions Centres and re-determined every February.
notes: Read the right table. The IBAS schedule is the more precise-looking one and it is not yours: it converts 24.00 to 64.40 where the table that applies to a candidate sitting the IB in Denmark converts 24 to 64.60, and the gap widens in the thirties.

Because you are converted from a whole number, every single point is a step. There is no partial credit for being high within a grade band, which is precisely what the Australian-sat IBAS schedule exists to give.

The Combined Rank travels even though the application does not. UAC only runs admissions for New South Wales and the ACT, but the conversion is national, so a rank quoted by a university in Perth means the same thing.
The schedule is republished annually and the values move. A table on a coaching site, or one remembered from a sibling's year, is the wrong table by definition.

Named prerequisite subjects sit on top of the rank - typically mathematics at a specified level for engineering, economics and science, and chemistry or biology for health degrees. Whether an SL subject satisfies a prerequisite is decided by the university, not by UAC.

portal.name: UAC for New South Wales and the ACT, where an IB Diploma makes you eligible; direct to the university everywhere else

deadlines.label: IB results released
deadlines.notes: Results reach the candidate on 6 July 2027, the IB's usual results day, not yet confirmed by the IB for 2027. An earlier date sometimes quoted is the IB's transcript-request cut-off, a separate IB deadline. UAC's IB applicants page (https://www.uac.edu.au/future-applicants/admission-criteria/ib-applicants) gives no May-session release date; its only date is for the November session, when UAC will notify NSW and ACT applicants of their IB Admissions Score "via email on Friday 18 December 2026". Denmark sits the May session, which is why a July 2027 start is tight and February 2028 is the realistic main option.

deadlines.label: Semester 1 2028 (main intake)
deadlines.notes: 2028 teaching dates are set one university at a time; there is no national one. The Australian National University's published university calendar for 2028 gives "Semester 1 begins — 21 Feb" and "Semester 1 ends — 26 May", so expect late February. Other universities will differ by a week or two and you must check the one you are applying to. There is likewise no national application deadline: international applications generally open around a year ahead and many universities accept them until a few weeks before teaching starts, subject to visa processing time, which is the constraint that actually binds. This is the main Australian intake and the realistic one for a May 2027 IB candidate.

deadlines.label: Semester 2 2027 (mid-year intake)
deadlines.notes: As with Semester 1 2028, the dates are published but only institution by institution. The Australian National University's 2027 calendar gives "Semester 2 begins — 26 Jul" and "Semester 2 ends — 29 Oct". That is the option that gets you started soonest after the May 2027 exams, and it is three weeks after IB results on 6 July 2027 — which is tight for an offer, a Confirmation of Enrolment and a subclass 500 visa in sequence, and is the reason February 2028 is the realistic choice rather than this one. Not every degree admits mid-year either; engineering, health and many professional degrees are Semester 1 only. Verify per degree and per university.

deadlines.label: Student visa (subclass 500) application
deadlines.notes: After you receive a Confirmation of Enrolment. You cannot apply until you hold a CoE from the university, and you must hold a valid CoE when the visa is decided. Allow several months.

steps: Decide first whether you want July 2027 or February 2028, then check whether the specific degree has a mid-year intake - this single choice changes your whole timeline, and engineering, health and most professional degrees are semester 1 only.

Convert your predicted IB total to a Combined Rank on UAC's current schedule, then look up the rank each degree requires. Some universities publish a guaranteed-entry rank, which turns the question into arithmetic.

Work out which route your state uses. For New South Wales and the ACT you may apply through UAC on one application and one fee; for Victoria, South Australia and Western Australia the state admissions centre will not take an IB candidate sitting the exams in Denmark, and Queensland's is unresolved, so you apply directly to each university.
Ask your school's IB Diploma coordinator to authorise the IB to release your results - to UAC if you are using it, and to each university if you are not. Your school does this, not you.
Submit predicted IB grades. Through UAC an international applicant receives a conditional offer about 48 hours later, which can be used for pre-visa assessment but not to enrol.
Accept the offer, pay the deposit, and take out Overseas Student Health Cover - it is a visa condition, not a university one.

Receive the Confirmation of Enrolment, then apply online for the Student visa subclass 500, paying from AUD 2,500 and showing AUD 29,710 of living costs, the first twelve months of tuition and about AUD 2,000 of travel.
Book accommodation - Australian universities house a much smaller share of students than British or American ones, and Sydney and Melbourne rentals are tight.
application.selectionNotes: Entry is overwhelmingly rank-based against a published threshold, plus subject prerequisites. A few degrees add an interview, portfolio or admissions test - medicine and dentistry in particular. Some universities publish guaranteed-entry ranks, which means an offer is automatic if you meet the number. There is no personal statement culture and no essay for most degrees. Whether a conditional offer on predicted grades is normal for a direct application, as it is through UAC, is worth asking each university about.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: The whole system. Every bachelor's degree here is taught in English.
language.englishProof: Universities accept the IB Diploma with English A as evidence of English for most courses, and the subclass 500 visa also has its own English requirement. Exact IELTS and TOEFL thresholds vary by university and by course - typical minimums are IELTS 6.5 overall with no band below 6.0.
notes: The visa English requirement and the university English requirement are separate. Meeting the university's does not automatically satisfy Home Affairs - check the subclass 500 English criteria.

tuitionEuEea.value: Not applicable - Australia has no EU/EEA fee category, and Commonwealth Supported Places are for Australian and New Zealand citizens only. You pay full international fees.

tuitionNonEu.value: Roughly AUD 47,000-57,000 a year at a major research university for arts, design and business, with medicine, dentistry and veterinary science substantially higher. Verified example: UNSW Sydney's 2026 international rates are AUD 985 per unit of credit for Arts, AUD 1,000 for Design, AUD 1,090 for Architecture and AUD 1,180 for Accounting and Actuarial Studies, and a standard full-time year is 48 units of credit - so about AUD 47,300 for Arts and AUD 56,600 for Business.

costs.applicationFee: Most Australian universities charge either no application fee or AUD 100-150 for international direct applications. State admissions centres (UAC, VTAC, QTAC, SATAC) charge their own processing fees. Check each university's own fee.

livingCostMonthly.value: The Department of Home Affairs requires evidence of AUD 29,710 in living costs for twelve months for a single student - about AUD 2,476 a month. Home Affairs states plainly that this is the visa minimum and that actual living costs vary across Australia and may be much higher.

notes: The AUD 29,710 is living costs only. On top you must show the first twelve months of course fees and about AUD 2,000 for travel to and from Australia if you are applying from Europe.

As an alternative to savings you may instead show that a parent or partner had a personal annual income of at least AUD 87,856 in the twelve months before you apply, evidenced by official tax documents - bank statements are not accepted.
Student visa subclass 500 application charge: from AUD 2,500 as of September 2026.
Overseas Student Health Cover is compulsory for the full length of the visa and is charged separately by the insurer.
Universities also charge a Student Services and Amenities Fee on top of tuition.
Not established: whether tuition can rise between years of the same degree, and by how much. Ask in writing before you accept.

funding: University international scholarships. Most Australian universities publish entrance scholarships for international undergraduates, usually a percentage discount on tuition (often 10-25%) awarded automatically on your admission score or by separate application. Amounts vary - check each university's scholarship page when you apply.
Destination Australia and similar government-funded schemes support study at regional campuses; these are aimed at moving students outside Sydney and Melbourne and can be substantial.
Faculty-specific awards, particularly in engineering and science, awarded after first year on results.

Part-time work. The visa allows up to 48 hours a fortnight during teaching periods and unrestricted hours in scheduled breaks, and Australian minimum wages are high by European standards - but you cannot count on work income for the visa financial test, which explicitly requires you to show funds without relying on employment in Australia.

funding.note: A full degree outside the EU/EEA follows separate rules, with its own ties-to-Denmark form: check su.dk before budgeting.

funding: There is no Australian government loan scheme for international undergraduates.
workRights: On a Student visa subclass 500 you may work up to 48 hours per fortnight while your course of study or training is in session, and without limit during scheduled course breaks. After you graduate, the Temporary Graduate visa (subclass 485), Post-Higher Education Work stream, is for international students with a recent degree from an Australian institution and usually allows a stay of between two and three years depending on the qualification. You must be 35 or under when you apply, and you must have held a Student visa within the previous six months. Sources: https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/visas/getting-a-visa/visa-listing/student-500 and https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/visas/getting-a-visa/visa-listing/temporary-graduate-485
residency: You need a Student visa, subclass 500. Apply online after the university issues a Confirmation of Enrolment, and you must still hold a valid CoE when the visa is decided. Requirements include Overseas Student Health Cover, the genuine student criterion, health and character checks, and the financial evidence above. The visa allows a stay of up to six years in line with your enrolment, and the application charge is from AUD 2,500. Student visa applications lodged outside Australia are processed under a Ministerial Direction - Direction 115 for applications lodged on or after 14 November 2025 - which prioritises some applications over others, so processing time is not simply first-come-first-served. Source: https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/visas/getting-a-visa/visa-listing/student-500
housing: Australian universities house a much smaller share of students than American or British ones, so most international students rent privately or take a place in a purpose-built student accommodation block. Sydney and Melbourne are expensive and competitive; Adelaide, Hobart, Wollongong and Canberra are easier. Apply for university residential colleges as soon as you accept an offer, and budget well above the AUD 29,710 visa minimum if you want to live in inner Sydney.
healthcare: Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC) is a condition of the subclass 500 visa and must cover the whole length of the visa. You buy it from an approved Australian insurer, usually through the university at the point of accepting your offer. The EHIC is not valid in Australia. If you are a Norwegian or Swedish citizen covered by your own country's scheme, you may be exempt from OSHC under special arrangements: check with the Department of Home Affairs before you buy it. Denmark has no such arrangement.

institutions.name: University of Melbourne
institutions.englishBachelors: Uses the 'Melbourne Model': broad three-year undergraduate degrees (Arts, Science, Commerce, Design, Biomedicine) followed by a professional master's for law, engineering, medicine or teaching.
institutions.note: Broad bachelor's degrees first, then a professional master's, as in much of Europe. Law, medicine and engineering are graduate entry, which suits students not ready to pick a profession at 18.

institutions.name: University of Sydney
institutions.englishBachelors: Three-year bachelor's degrees with a shared open-learning component, plus combined degrees and direct-entry professional programmes.
institutions.note: A sandstone campus near central Sydney. It publishes guaranteed-entry ranks for many degrees, so you can check them against your predicted IB conversion.

institutions.name: Australian National University
institutions.englishBachelors: Three- and four-year degrees with a strong research-led first year and unusually small cohorts for a national university.
institutions.note: A research university in the capital, next to the institutions its politics students study. Canberra is small, cold by Australian standards and much cheaper than Sydney.

institutions.name: University of Queensland
institutions.englishBachelors: Broad three-year degrees plus dual programmes; strong life and environmental sciences.
institutions.note: A riverside campus in subtropical Brisbane with strong life-sciences research. Living costs are noticeably lower than in Sydney or Melbourne.

institutions.name: Monash University
institutions.englishBachelors: Large faculty-based degrees with direct entry to professional programmes including medicine, pharmacy and engineering straight from school.
institutions.note: Lets you enter professional degrees such as medicine and engineering straight from school. Melbourne makes them graduate entry; Monash also has a campus in Malaysia and a study centre in Prato, Italy.

institutions.name: UNSW Sydney
institutions.englishBachelors: Runs a three-term calendar rather than two semesters, so there are more entry points and a faster path through the degree.
institutions.note: Publishes its international fees per unit of credit, which makes budgeting simple. In 2026 that was AUD 985 for Arts up to AUD 1,180 for Accounting, on a 48-unit year.

institutions.name: University of Western Australia
institutions.englishBachelors: Broad three-year bachelor's degrees followed by professional master's, similar in shape to Melbourne.
institutions.note: Strong in earth sciences and marine biology, in Perth. Perth shares a time zone with much of Asia but is a very long way from everywhere else.

institutions.name: Adelaide University
institutions.englishBachelors: Bachelor's degrees across seven campuses in South Australia, including engineering, health and agricultural and wine science.
institutions.note: Opened in January 2026, replacing the University of Adelaide and UniSA. It teaches across seven campuses in South Australia, and international students apply to it directly.

institutions.name: University of Technology Sydney
institutions.englishBachelors: Practice-oriented degrees with compulsory industry placements in several programmes.
institutions.note: Applied, industry-facing teaching on a campus in central Sydney. Entry ranks are usually lower than at the Group of Eight universities.

institutions.name: RMIT University
institutions.englishBachelors: Design, engineering and technology degrees with strong studio and workshop teaching, plus a campus in Vietnam.
institutions.note: Strong in design, architecture and applied engineering, in the middle of Melbourne. A good fit if you want practice rather than research.

institutions.name: Queensland University of Technology
institutions.englishBachelors: Applied degrees branded 'the university for the real world', with work-integrated learning across most programmes.
institutions.note: Strong in robotics and the creative industries, at lower entry ranks. Living costs are lower than in Sydney or Melbourne; apply directly, since whether QTAC takes an offshore IB candidate is unresolved.

institutions.name: University of Wollongong
institutions.englishBachelors: Mid-sized campus university 80 km south of Sydney, with strong engineering and computing.
institutions.note: A research university in a beach town, with much cheaper rent than Sydney. It counts as a regional location for some scholarship and post-study work purposes, so check whether your campus qualifies.

institutions.name: Macquarie University
institutions.englishBachelors: Flexible degrees with a built-in professional placement unit, on a parkland campus next to a major business district.
institutions.note: In Sydney's technology corridor, with good internship access. Entry ranks are more achievable than at USyd or UNSW for the same subjects.

institutions.name: Deakin University
institutions.englishBachelors: Multi-campus, with a large online and blended offering alongside on-campus degrees.
institutions.note: Accessible entry requirements, and sport science, nutrition and cyber security among its degrees. The Geelong campuses are much cheaper to live near than central Melbourne.

institutions.name: University of Tasmania
institutions.englishBachelors: Bachelor's degrees across arts, science, business, health and marine and Antarctic studies, with campuses in Hobart, Launceston and Burnie.
institutions.note: Treats a completed IB Diploma as meeting its general entry requirements and can collect your results from the IB if your coordinator gives permission.

institutions.name: Griffith University
institutions.englishBachelors: More than 200 degrees open to international students, on campuses in Brisbane and on the Gold Coast.
institutions.note: Converts an IB Diploma into a Combined Rank for entry, the same national rank the other universities here use. International students apply to it directly.

institutions.name: Curtin University
institutions.englishBachelors: Bachelor's degrees in engineering, mining, health, business, design and the sciences at its main campus in Perth.
institutions.note: Asks for a full IB Diploma with at least 24 points in six subjects, and marks its more competitive courses at 31 to 39 points. International students apply directly.
